result.title: When Momentum Helps Polyak--Ruppert Averaging
result.summary: Polyak--Ruppert averaging gives SGD and momentum methods the same asymptotic covariance. We characterize how fast finite runs reach it and how far they can be parallelized. For strongly convex quadratics with additive noise, we prove an online--offline bridge: the empirical risk minimizer on the samples of a tail average is one Newton step from the tail-averaged query point of any online procedure. For SGD, heavy ball, and Nesterov's method with constant momentum, this step is a boundary term at the two ends of the tail and splits the gap to the offline estimator into center, covariance, and shape errors. Necessary and sufficient conditions show that, on the least curved direction, the center error sets the pace: SGD needs $m\ggκ^2$ rounds but momentum only $m\ggκ$, where $κ$ is the condition number, so at sample size $N$ the critical batch size grows from $Θ(\sqrt{N}/κ)$ to $Θ(\sqrt{N/κ})$. The covariance error separates the momentum methods: heavy ball has relative variance excess $Θ(κ^{3/2}/m)$ along the stiffest direction, whereas Nesterov has relative error $O(\sqrtκ/m)$ in every direction. The shape error is method-independent by a Berry--Esseen bound uniform in $κ$ and batch size, so confidence intervals are valid when the other two errors vanish. We further examine how the conclusions change under heavy-tailed or state-dependent noise and clipping, and establish a first-order comparison with ERM for nonlinear Nesterov averaging under explicit conditions.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 Polyak–Ruppert 平均在有限步运行时逼近离线估计的速度与可并行化上限：对带噪声的强凸二次问题给出在线–离线桥，把与 ERM 的差距拆成 center、covariance、shape 三项误差，并给出 SGD、Heavy Ball、Nesterov 的充要条件、临界批大小标度，以及在重尾或状态相关噪声和裁剪下的变化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其对迭代平均的偏差–方差分解、临界批大小与噪声依赖的分析语言，可能为并行采样多条 latent 推理轨迹后的状态聚合方式与并行收益上限提供形式化参照，是否可迁移需核查原文假设。
